concept: mlx.launch jaccl backend flags and hostfile coordinator handling
summary: Backend selection falls back from `--backend` to the hostfile backend field, then to nccl when CUDA is available, else ring

facts.text: Backend selection falls back from `--backend` to the hostfile backend field, then to nccl when CUDA is available, else ring
`launch_jaccl` sets `MLX_JACCL_COORDINATOR` to the first IP of rank 0 plus `--starting-port` (default 32323)
The launcher errors if rank 0 lists no IP, if rdma list length differs from host count, or if a host's own rdma slot is not null
For jaccl-ring the launcher checks only neighbour pairs (i-1) mod n and (i+1) mod n; for jaccl mesh it checks all pairs
`jaccl-ring` sets `MLX_JACCL_RING=1`; both modes write the rdma matrix to a remote temp file exported as `MLX_IBV_DEVICES`
The remote launch script exports `--env` entries in order, then temp-file variables, then `MLX_RANK`, and finally `exec`s the command
Hostfile `envs` are prepended to `--env`, so command-line values override them
`--connections-per-ip` is read only by the ring backend launcher, not by the JACCL one
Wrapping `mlx_lm share` in `mlx.launch` hangs or fails silently according to the mlx-lm issue 955 author, who says its built-in launcher must be used
The MLX docs recommend `mlx.distributed_config --auto-setup --backend jaccl --over thunderbolt` to produce the hostfile
